WHAT WAS READ. In this print, the foot of the band's shadow, traced every 10 px across x 590-780, runs from y 113 to 78 (slope 0.186), so it reaches the horizon (y 496) at x -1473, inside the -1380 to -1760 the four lines read before. This camera's principal point at x 0 was put there by T-3166 ("the principal point therefore stands at the print's left edge") and was not measured: level fronts fix the horizon but not where along it the point stands. So this print alone reads a 45-degree wall only through an assumed point; with the point at about x -1470 the same line is the south flank. In the partial view (glessner_partial, solved by T-3168: principal point x -50, horizontal focal 836 px, yaw -80), 1828's porch, cornice and corner render within about 10 px. There the same band's foot, traced every 10 px across x 245-365, runs from y 323 to 283 and reaches that camera's horizon (y 489) between x -250 and -320. So the solved camera reads the wall as 1824's south flank, the one the sheet places and the build stands. Rendered through that camera (carried into 1824's frame by the 1904 placements, eye u 34.66, v -19.07), the build's flank eave falls along the band within about 15-20 px. WINDOWS: the partial view shows openings in that flank's upper storey (about x 250-262 and 300-317, round-headed, with a third doubtful at the damaged edge x 365-385), where the build has its two columns (x 280 and 363). This print shows the stretch next to the bay blank under the band, with three dark arch-topped shapes at x 700-755, y 356-436 that may be openings or the trees' shadows. So the two pictures disagree on the flank's openings as well as on its direction, and the build keeps the sheet's flank with its windows (L-k01-1824-marsh-1887).
